title: The Morning Digest: September 28, 2026
dek: "A ~275 kb/d Midwest (PADD 2) heavy-crude buyer is back online. Meanwhile Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap, and Ukraine's campaign against Russian refineries hit its biggest weekend of 2026."

claims.text: The call: Joliet is back.
The call: The de-escalation bid died over the weekend.
The call: Ukraine's refining-strike campaign had its biggest weekend of 2026.

Flat price: Friday settled on diplomacy hopes: Brent Nov $104.32, WTI Nov $92.41 (both ~-2.2%). Sunday's reopen priced the failed roadmap: Brent ~$106 - 108, WTI ~$93 - 95. Brent is up ~18% in September.
Flat price: The curve stays deeply backwardated  -  near-term physical tightness, normalization further out. Brent - WTI prompt ≈ $11.9, still wide; WTI is the cheaper length.

Middle East: roadmap rejected, waterway healing: Iran's seven-day plan, delivered via Qatar at UNGA: reopen the strait within seven days in exchange for lifting the naval blockade, easing oil-export sanctions, releasing ~$12B in frozen assets, and a regional ceasefire. Trump: "not acceptable." Iran says no formal rejection reached Tehran through official channels...

Middle East: roadmap rejected, waterway healing: Trump reportedly told reporters Saturday he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms. Sunday reporting: talks could continue this week with Qatar mediating.

Middle East: roadmap rejected, waterway healing: Harassment stepped up: Iran reportedly targeted 19 ships attempting authorized routes in 48h; the IRGC claimed it attacked and seized the small Togo-flagged product tanker Trend; UKMTO confirmed a tanker struck near Khasab. The premium now runs through freight and insurance, not just blocked flow.

Middle East: roadmap rejected, waterway healing: Underneath it, the physical picture improves. Hormuz oil flows are back to ~13.5 mb/d (7-day average), about two-thirds of prewar ~20 mb/d. Saudi Gulf loadings hit 5.28 mb/d Sept 1 - 23, the strongest since the war began. The East-West pipeline restart stands at a reduced rate  -  but the weekend's Houthi attacks on Yan...

Middle East: roadmap rejected, waterway healing: Yemen/Red Sea escalated: the heaviest Houthi salvo against Saudi Arabia since July  -  missiles toward Khamis Mushait, drones toward Riyadh, all intercepted; the Houthis claimed hits on Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
Middle East: roadmap rejected, waterway healing: OPEC+ left October output unchanged; the next meeting is Oct 4. The 2027 quota/baseline review is the item to watch.

Ukraine/Russia: four plants in four days: Saturday: Ilsky (Krasnodar, ~130 kb/d) halted  -  drones hit three primary units and the tank farm (Ukrainian General Staff; governor confirms). Friday: Lukoil's Perm (~252 kb/d) halted and Novoshakhtinsk knocked offline (both single-source, unconfirmed independently). Overnight Sunday: the largest one-night drone bar...

Ukraine/Russia: four plants in four days: The read: escalation → distillate tightness. Refining capacity is being knocked out faster than it repairs, into a global distillate market at record stress  -  US retail diesel at an all-time high. Crude export impact is second-order: refinery hits cut crude demand more than supply.

Ukraine/Russia: four plants in four days: The EU's new sanctions package (proposal stage, needs unanimity) would sanction third-country ports Kulevi (Georgia) and Karimun (Indonesia)  -  the first time the EU would target third-country ports  -  and von der Leyen floated replacing the G7 price cap with a full maritime-services ban on Russian crude. Cracks and the heavy complex: Distillate is the shortage: ICE gasoil cracked ~$95/bbl vs ~$74 in August; NY Harbor ULSD hit a record $113.48 on Sept 16 (RBN Energy flagged); the 3-2-1 is ~$75. Rising distillate cracks make SCO relatively more valuable  -  the SYN - WCS dislocation widens into winter.

Cracks and the heavy complex: The blended-heavy arb window is open (+$5.51/bbl modeled incentive), reclassifying heavy toward light pools at the margin  -  a softener on the WCS diff if Joliet's return is already priced.

Venezuela: the comp barrel: US imports of Venezuelan crude (w/e Sept 18): 583 kb/d, down from 782  -  Chevron-licensed barrels into the USGC. Next weekly ~Sept 30.
Venezuela: the comp barrel: Production: OPEC MOMR July secondary-source 1,117 kb/d vs PDVSA's direct 1,200  -  treat the direct number with skepticism. The September MOMR isn't out.

Venezuela: the comp barrel: Merey pricing: October cargo offers widened from ~−$14 to ~−$19/bbl vs Brent through September  -  driven by freight, not fundamentals: Aframax Jose - USGC hit a $3.5M lump sum (~$7/bbl equivalent). Distressed Merey length prices down to clear against WCS and other heavies, or goes to storage as overhang  -  either way th...

Venezuela: the comp barrel: Forward: WSJ reports the Pentagon-backed NABEP consortium has 60 rigs and 70 pieces of equipment lined up, with two rigs departing Houston today for Venezuela. Rystad's upside case takes Venezuela to 1.6 mb/d by 2028  -  on more than $100B and a rig count that was 2 in August. Plans, not barrels  -  history wins.
Venezuela: the comp barrel: Sanctions/licenses: no weekend changes. Chevron licensed; Vitol/Trafigura moving the stored-crude deal under OFAC licenses.
